met_analysis:
The Deep Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 06 kmph during past 06 hours and lies centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 16th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 11.2°N and Longitude 86.4°E, about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 700 km east- southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 910 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of today, the 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni, by noon of 20th November, 2026 as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sikkim & neighbourhood persists and now extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian Sea off Kerala coast now lies over Southeast Arabian Sea & adjoining north Kerala coast at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over south Konkan & neighbourhoodat 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The east-west trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with the Deep Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal to northern parts of Maldives extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The Western Disturbance as a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along long 80°E to the north of Lat 28°N has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
